title: I Recorded the Warehouse Pallet-Jack Hour the Supervisor Called Idle

parts.text: I logged pallet-jack 7 from 2:00 to 3:00 for a live unload. The supervisor marked the hour idle and assigned me a write-up for standing. The equipment log he designed said: JACK TIME FOLLOWS THE SCAN. IDLE REQUIRES A ZERO SCAN. I was thirty-one, picker, holding a scan history of 42 pallets. Supervisor Grant said, "I didn't see motion." I pointed at the log. He shrugged. "Eyes beat scans." I photographed the 42 scans, the log, and the idle mark. Then I recorded the dock camera timestamp of the unload. At 3:08 HR asked why Grant's name was on a false-idle ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: HR can see 42 scans and dock video against an idle mark Grant entered.

social.video_title: He called a 42-pallet hour idle — Part 1/2
social.description: Write-up, a jack log he designed, and eyes versus scans. I sent dock video. Would you have signed the idle?

parts.text: Grant called it a misclick until HR played the dock. I printed the ticket, the log, and a still. The write-up vanished. Grant told the break cage the log was always about optics. Optics is a word supervisors use when 42 is a number. Jack policy now has a second line: EYES DO NOT BEAT SCANS. I unload. Grant clicks less. The hour finally matches the pallets.

social.video_title: Eyes do not beat scans — Part 2/2
social.description: False-idle ticket, a dead write-up, and a second line on the log. Was standing ever 42 pallets?
